THIS WEEK IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT

The Wausau Common Council voted 8-2 to shut down the city's Flock license plate reader camera system over privacy concerns, the week's sharpest action across central Wisconsin meeting rooms.

  • The Wausau Common Council voted 8-2 to direct staff to cease using Flock camera data and physically cover all Flock license plate reader cameras within two business weeks.
  • The Wausau Finance Committee accepted a clean 2025 audit from new firm Maldin Jenkins CPAs, with one minor finding tied to suspension and debarment recordkeeping.
  • The Wausau Common Council directed the city to pursue five structural stormwater best-management practices plus water quality trading to meet Wisconsin River pollution limits.
  • The Weston Community Life & Public Safety Committee voted to instruct the DOT to include a Newport Avenue pedestrian crosswalk in Business 51 reconstruction plans, with one dissenting vote.
  • The Weston Parks and Recreation Committee unanimously recommended the Machm Miller Park master plan to the Village Board.
  • The Wausau School Board is set to have adopted a 2026-27 district tax levy of $44,385,271 at its October 26 special meeting, outcomes of which were not yet confirmed.

Coming up: The Wausau School Board holds a closed session Monday at 5 p.m. for a pupil expulsion hearing; later in the week, Wednesday brings a City of Wausau Economic Development Committee meeting at 5:15 p.m. and Thursday features a Police & Fire Commission special meeting at 7:30 a.m. and a Health & Human Services Committee session at Marathon County.
